series: Climate Fiscal Policy Brief No. 4.3 · October 2026
title: Codify Sustainability-Linked Sovereign Lending, Then Give It Scale

slides.title: Codify Sustainability-Linked Sovereign Lending, Then Give It Scale
slides.subtitle: Standard indicators, verification and pricing, and a reward bigger than an interest margin
slides.message: Sustainability-linked debt pays governments for national climate results, but each deal is handmade and small. Codify it, pay the reward from outside, and make guarantee capacity the prize.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.title: Four things keep sustainability-linked debt small

points.text: Each issuer invents its own indicators, baselines and step; the market standards say how to disclose them, not what they should be.
Corporate issuers miss them only 14–39% of the time. A reward paid whatever happens buys nothing.
Uruguay's 2025 methane result is verified in 2028; the last reward is applied in 2037.
The market norm is 25 bp per target, with no link to what the policy costs.

slides.source: Feldhütter, Halskov and Krebbers (2024); Stewart and Ul Haq (2023); Climate Bonds Initiative (2024); Uruguay MEF (2023).

slides.title: A bond whose coupon moves with results gives the government commitment, not money

points.lead: Investors price the expected step at issue.
points.text: Bond prices track the size of the penalty, with no mispricing.

points.lead: So the government pays for its own reward,
points.text: plus a premium for the uncertainty. It still gains from meeting the target once the bond is sold: a commitment device.
whose benefits mostly go abroad. Uruguay's bond can cut its coupon by up to about $40m, but bondholders priced that in.
An intermediary lends on a fixed coupon and refunds interest for verified results; it bears the risk across many countries.

slides.source: Lefournier (2023); Feldhütter et al. (2024); Estevão, Stretton and Zimmermann (2024). Working paper 4.3, Proposition 2.

slides.title: Codify the loan: write it once, use it many times

points.text: outturns national statistics already report: emissions, methane per kg of beef, forest area, clean power share, carbon price.
the country's own Paris pledge plus a published margin, with a peer-based floor.
a named verifier checks the national inventory, as UNDP does for Uruguay.
a published reward per unit of outperformance, stated per tonne of CO₂, so a funder can compare indicators and countries.

slides.source: Working paper 4.3, Section 4 and Appendix A; World Bank Group Evolution Roadmap (2022) calls for standardized buy-downs.

slides.title: The leverage is real only where the guarantee is honored and used

points.text: the base case needs the guarantor's claims honored like development bank loans, through a counter-indemnity.
at high call rates the multiple falls toward one; give account credits instead.
capacity is worth nothing to a country with no green borrowing to guarantee.
the government's liability becomes smaller, contingent and contracted, not zero.
a reward offset by less concessional finance elsewhere pays nothing.

items.text: the instrument can be repeated cheaply.
a rebate cannot pay for a major reform.
80 times the incentive per dollar on the record, 2.7 under stress.
publish an indicator menu, baselines, verification rules and a price per tonne.
back a fixed-coupon intermediary that refunds interest for verified results.
make guarantee capacity the prize and fund its buffer (Briefs 4.1, 4.2).
